title: Atrial Fibrillation Anticoagulation Pathway
description: Evidence-based treatment pathway for anticoagulation in non-valvular atrial fibrillation.
source_description: 2023 ACC/AHA/ACCP/HRS Guideline for Diagnosis and Management of Atrial Fibrillation. Circulation 2024;149(1):e1-e156.

contraindication_warnings.active_major_bleeding: Active major bleeding is an absolute contraindication to anticoagulation. Address bleeding source first.
contraindication_warnings.severe_thrombocytopenia: Platelet count <50,000/uL — anticoagulation risk may outweigh benefit. Hematology consult recommended.

steps.name: Assess stroke risk
steps.description: Calculate CHA2DS2-VASc score to determine stroke risk and need for anticoagulation.

decision_points.note: Anticoagulation may be considered; assess additional risk modifiers (AF burden, LA size, obesity, eGFR <45)

steps.name: Assess bleeding risk
steps.description: Calculate HAS-BLED score to identify modifiable bleeding risk factors. Per 2023 ACC/AHA guideline, bleeding risk scores should NOT be used to withhold anticoagulation — use them to address modifiable factors and guide monitoring intensity.

decision_points.note: High bleeding risk — address modifiable factors (hypertension, labile INR, alcohol, NSAIDs), increase monitoring frequency. Do NOT withhold anticoagulation based on score alone.

steps.name: Assess renal function
steps.description: Calculate CrCl (Cockcroft-Gault) for DOAC dose adjustment. CrCl is preferred over eGFR for DOAC dosing as clinical trials used Cockcroft-Gault.

decision_points.note: Some DOACs require dose adjustment; check edoxaban CrCl >95 contraindication
Limited DOAC options; dabigatran contraindicated below CrCl 30 without specific P-gp considerations

steps.name: First-line: DOAC therapy
steps.description: DOACs are preferred over warfarin for most patients with non-valvular AF (Class 1 recommendation). Apixaban, rivaroxaban, dabigatran, or edoxaban.

options.reduced_dose_criteria: Need 2 of 3: age >= 80, weight <= 60 kg, or serum creatinine >= 1.5 mg/dL

options.standard_dose: 20 mg PO daily with evening meal
options.reduced_dose: 15 mg PO daily with evening meal

options.reduced_dose_criteria: CrCl 15-30 mL/min (any patient), OR CrCl 30-50 mL/min with concomitant dronedarone or systemic ketoconazole
options.note: Contraindicated if CrCl < 15 mL/min. Avoid P-gp inhibitors entirely at CrCl 15-30. Other P-gp inhibitors (verapamil, amiodarone, quinidine) do NOT require dose adjustment at CrCl > 30.

options.reduced_dose_criteria: CrCl 15-50 mL/min, weight <= 60 kg, or concomitant P-gp inhibitors (verapamil, quinidine, certain macrolides)
options.note: FDA BOXED WARNING: Do NOT use if CrCl > 95 mL/min — reduced efficacy vs warfarin in ENGAGE AF-TIMI 48 trial.

steps.name: Reduced renal function: Limited DOAC options
steps.description: CrCl 15-29 mL/min. Apixaban and rivaroxaban have data in this range. Dabigatran is contraindicated below CrCl 30 (no dosing recommendation). Warfarin is an alternative.

options.medication: Apixaban 5 mg BID (or 2.5 mg BID if dose-reduction criteria met)
Rivaroxaban 15 mg daily with evening meal

steps.name: Severe CKD / Dialysis: Warfarin or apixaban
steps.description: CrCl < 15 mL/min or on dialysis. Rivaroxaban, dabigatran, and edoxaban are NOT recommended for ESKD/dialysis (insufficient evidence). Apixaban 5 mg BID (FDA-approved for HD) has limited data. Warfarin is the traditional choice. Shared decision-making essential.

options.medication: Apixaban 5 mg BID (FDA-approved in ESKD; limited data from RENAL-AF trial)
